title: Roots-of-unity comparison: transition compatibility and isomorphism along isomorphisms
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and for $N\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$ let $c^f_{\mu_N}:f^{-1}\mu_{N,Y}\to\mu_{N,X}$ be the inverse-image comparison map of the pro-etale sheaves of $N$-th roots of unity [def-pur-roots-of-unity-inverse-image, def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf], and $c^f_{\mathbf Z/N}:f^{-1}(\mathbf Z/N\mathbf Z)_Y\to(\mathbf Z/N\mathbf Z)_X$ the structure map of constant sheaves [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Then:

1. For $N\mid N'$ and the transition maps $t_{N',N}:u\mapsto u^{N'/N}$ of [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf], $t_{N',N}\circ c^f_{\mu_{N'}}=c^f_{\mu_N}\circ f^{-1}(t_{N',N})$; so for a prime $\ell$ the maps $c^f_{\mu_{\ell^r}}$, $r\geq1$, form a morphism of inverse systems $(f^{-1}\mu_{\ell^r,Y})_r\to(\mu_{\ell^r,X})_r$.
2. $c^f_{\mu_N}$ is semilinear over $c^f_{\mathbf Z/N}$: $c^f_{\mu_N}(a\cdot u)=c^f_{\mathbf Z/N}(a)\cdot c^f_{\mu_N}(u)$ for local sections $a$ of $f^{-1}(\mathbf Z/N\mathbf Z)_Y$ and $u$ of $f^{-1}\mu_{N,Y}$, the module structures being those of [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf].
3. If $f$ is an isomorphism of schemes, then $c^f_{\mu_N}$ is an isomorphism of sheaves of abelian groups; under the identification $(f^{-1}\mathcal F)(U\xrightarrow{u}X)\cong\mathcal F(U\xrightarrow{f\circ u}Y)$ of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] (1) it is the identity of $\{v\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)^\times:v^N=1\}$.

proof.text: For each section, the chosen roots-section equivalence satisfies its inclusion normalization. Evaluate kernel.lift_ι to identify the transition with the (N'/N)-th power. The chosen direct-image root map satisfies its projection formula. Pullback of functions commutes with powers, giving the direct-image transition square. Transpose it by Adjunction.homEquiv_naturality_right_square. NatTrans.ofOpSequence constructs the tower map from the consecutive-power squares. These calculations are the proved private lemmas roots_sections_inclusion, roots_transition_inclusion, roots_transition_value, roots_direct_formula, roots_direct_transition, roots_inverse_transition and roots_tower_map.

First prove that the actual inverse-image abelian sheaf F is killed by N. Direct image is additive sectionwise, so its left adjoint is additive by Adjunction.left_adjoint_additive. Apply it to N times the identity equals zero and evaluate on sections. The canonical constant Z/N comparison c is invertible: use finiteCoefficientInverseImageMap_constant and the invertibility of both finiteCoefficientConstantComparison maps and finiteCoefficientInverseImageMap. Pull the canonical torsionSheafModuleStructure on F back along c to construct the required action on the fixed inverse-image groups. Restrictions are semilinear by naturality of c. For the unit clause, form the direct image of this action and restrict scalars along the actual RingCat adjunction unit. Any such restricted action is normalized on integer constants because ring maps preserve integer casts and Int.cast_smul_eq_zsmul holds for every module. Apply torsionSheaf_hom_linear on Y to the AddCommGrpCat unit. For uniqueness, restrict any proposed action along c inverse. The same integer-cast argument and its restriction hypothesis make this a normalized constant Z/N action. Uniqueness in existsUnique_constantZModSheafModuleStructure identifies it with the canonical action; evaluate at c(a), cancel c followed by its inverse, and use Module.ext' and function extensionality. This proves existsUnique_proEtaleRootsOfUnityInverseImageAction without a new hole. For the root comparison, restrict its given source action along c inverse, prove the same normalization and N-torsion, and apply torsionSheaf_hom_linear on X. Evaluate at c(a) and cancel the inverse composite to obtain semilinearity for every local scalar. The calculation needs only restriction compatibility, so the unit normalization is not additionally used for this last clause.

For an isomorphism f, use the inverse of the recorded comma-normalized inverse-image identification. Its specification expresses it as the unit followed by restriction along the distinguished comma arrow. The adjunction unit followed by the root comparison is the direct-image root map. Naturality of the comparison and the inclusion give the restriction formula on root values. The direct-image projection formula and pullback.lift_fst show that this root value is unchanged. The two roots-section equivalences are injective, so this proves identity on roots under the recorded identification. Their bijectivity makes every component of the comparison bijective. ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective, NatIso.isIso_of_isIso_app and reflection by sheafToPresheaf prove that the sheaf comparison is an isomorphism. No positivity or invertibility of N is used in these private lemmas.
